observation.visible_scene: A round wall clock with a black rim and mirror-reversed numerals (12 at top, 1-6 reading down the left side, 11-7 down the right side) hangs on a pale textured wall. In the lower foreground, a static heap of glossy multicolored Christmas-light bulbs (red, blue, teal, yellow, white) rests on a cream woven surface. The clock shows three hands: a short black hand near the top, a long black hand, and a thin red hand. The framing of clock and bulbs is fixed across all frames, indicating a stationary camera.
visible_changes: The long black hand rotates steadily through the excerpt, sweeping from the 8 mark (lower right) down past 7, 6, 5 and ending near the 4 mark (lower left) by the last frame.

The thin red hand alternates orientation from frame to frame, pointing toward the right (9) on odd-indexed frames and toward the left (3) on even-indexed frames, i.e. it appears to flip 180 degrees every sample.
The short black hand at the top stays essentially fixed, pointing between the 11 and 12 positions.
The pile of bulbs, the wall, and the clock face do not move; no object translation, deformation, or occlusion change occurs.
outside_clip_unknowns: The real rotational speed and direction of the red hand and of the long black hand (the clock may be running fast / time-lapsed, and the red hand's per-frame flip may be sampling aliasing rather than true oscillation).
What the hands do before t=0 and after t=2.667s.
uncertain_details: Which hand is hour/minute/second is not determinable from the images.
Because the numerals are mirrored, the physical (real-time) sense of the black hand's sweep cannot be confirmed from the picture alone.
Whether the red hand's left/right alternation reflects genuine back-and-forth motion or a fast rotation captured at the clip's frame rate is ambiguous.
